newsletter:
══ SECTION 1: NEWSLETTER ══

Good morning. The macro tone is constructive but not clean — SPY sits 3.4% above its 50-day and 6.3% above its 200-day, VIX collapsed about 13% in 24 hours back into the high teens with the curve in contango, and the regime vote reads TRANSITIONAL at 6/10. Cross-asset says risk-on with caveats: copper is up 4% on the month, gold is off 7.4% (defensive bid unwinding), but the 10Y has climbed to 4.53% (+3.1% on the month) and DXY is firmer by 1.7%. That combination — softer gold, firmer dollar, higher yields, lower vol — typically supports cyclicals and growth equities but caps duration-sensitive plays and gold miners.

Leadership is clear and structurally meaningful: XLK is +6.0% on 21d and accelerating bullish, while XLV quietly leads at +5.2%. Tech leading with Health Care co-leading is a barbell — offense plus a defensive growth pocket — which historically signals the market wants quality earnings rather than pure beta. Semiconductors at +10.8% 21d and Software-Infrastructure accelerating confirm the tech engine is the index right now. The flip side: XLE, XLF, XLP, XLRE are all clustered near flat, so participation is narrower than the headline suggests (sector breadth above 50SMA is only 54.5%).

On the un-run side, the screen produced nothing meeting the coiling+bullish-flow filter today, which itself is information — the easy setups have already triggered. Names already extended are the obvious semis complex (SOXX/SMH constituents, NVDA, AVGO, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC) and Communication Equipment (ANET, CSCO) — these have run 12-13 months and are in ceiling territory per the heat reads. The fresher rotation read is into Consumer Electronics and Software-Infrastructure (acceleration prints of 2.25 and 1.99 respectively, but only +0.8% and +4.2% on 21d) — i.e., trajectory is turning up before price has extended. Nothing is rotating out yet, no flips, which means the tape is adding leadership rather than swapping it.

Into tomorrow, two things to watch: (1) the 10Y at 4.53% — another leg higher pressures the duration trade and could be the catalyst that finally cracks the extended semi/comm-equip names; (2) whether Software-Infrastructure (think MSFT, ORCL, PANW, NOW, FTNT) follows through — it's early in its heat cycle and the acceleration is real, making it the cleanest place to look for continuation rather than chasing semis. Keep sizing modest in the ceiling-flagged groups; lean toward the early-cycle accelerators.
